title: Embeddings/Rerank downgrade proxy: HTTP semantic preservation and pagination parity
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a downgrade proxy that accepts modern embeddings + rerank requests (streaming and non-streaming, structured outputs, function/tool-calling hints) and translates them to the legacy embed-rerank backend while preserving HTTP semantics, error codes, and pagination behavior. This proxy enables gradual migration for legacy clients and reduces emergency rollbacks when model variants or new response formats are introduced.
background: We have multiple incidents where new features (structured 'metadata' fields, function-calling hints, or streaming tokens) caused legacy clients to fail due to unexpected JSON shapes or new 5xx/429 semantics. The intent is to provide a translation layer that normalizes responses and maps error codes and pagination tokens to the legacy contract. Current related work: compatibility adapters in PM backlog and earlier ENG proxies, but none preserve HTTP-level details for streaming and retry semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts all inbound embeddings/rerank requests that conform to the new API surface and returns HTTP response codes that match the legacy contract for the client-facing path
Streaming responses must be convertible to legacy non-streaming and streaming behaviors depending on client headers (Accept: text/event-stream or legacy-stream flag)
Pagination tokens generated for legacy clients must be stable for identical query contexts and survive restarts within 72 hours
Error mapping table implemented: maps modern 5xx/4xx/429 with structured error payloads to legacy numeric codes and simple message formats; includes retry-after handling and idempotency hints
End-to-end tests covering edge cases: truncated KV cache responses, partial reranker failures, multi-model fallback scenarios
Performance overhead of proxy must be <5% added median latency at p50 for typical embed/rerank calls in staging
Canary rollout script exists with automatic rollback on increased error rate or latency regression (>2x baseline error-rate or >20% p95 latency increase)
Documentation and migration guide published in Confluence with example curl requests and sample client patch snippets
implementation_notes: Design: proxy lives in the routing mesh in front of legacy embed-rerank fleet. Two translation stages: request sanitization (strip unsupported tool-calling hints, normalize structured output requests) and response normalization (flatten structured fields into legacy 'items' list, map status codes). We'll reuse existing kernel for streaming chunk aggregation and the caching layer for token stability. Trade-offs: full fidelity of structured outputs can't be preserved for legacy clients; prefer safe degradation (drop unknown fields and attach a warning header).
error_mapping_summary: Mapping rules: modern 429 -> legacy 429 with X-Legacy-Retry-Hint header; modern structured 4xx (invalid_input) -> legacy 400 with short message; model-fallback 503 -> legacy 502 for downstream clients that expect gateway errors. For stream truncation, emit final chunk with code 'STREAM_TRUNCATED' in legacy message body and set HTTP 206 when partial content is returned.
pagination_strategy: Two-token scheme: proxy issues 'legacy_cursor_v1' tokens that encode (model, query_hash, offset, server_epoch). Token validation enforces server_epoch <= 72h; expired tokens return 410 with 'retry:reauth' semantics. For clients that pass modern 'cursor' we translate to legacy_cursor_v1 and populate Link headers for next/prev when applicable. Idempotency: POST embeddings requests include X-Request-ID fallback to compute deterministic cursor positions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for translation logic, integration tests against a dockerized legacy embed-rerank service, synthetic load tests for latency and token stability, and a canary in us-west-2 traffic slice with feature flag. Add contract tests: replay historical failing requests from incidents and assert normalized outputs. Create fuzz harness to generate malformed structured outputs and ensure safe degradation.
migration_playbook: 1) Deploy proxy in shadow mode to route 0% production traffic; 2) Enable response normalization in shadow and run contract tests; 3) Canary route 1-5% traffic for 24h with health checks; 4) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% if no regression; 5) Monitor token stability dashboard and errors; 6) Provide rollback toggle to forward traffic directly to legacy backend. Backout plan includes reissuing cursor epoch to invalidate new tokens if a severe bug escapes.
notes: Reviewed with PMs and Design 2026-02-27: agreed to prefer warning header + field-drop strategy over heavy transformations
Security checked: proxy must strip any tool-calling hooks before forwarding; KMS keys remain only in private plane
decisions: Keep cursor tokens opaque to clients but include readable metadata for debugging via admin endpoints
Map streaming-to-nonstream by buffering up to 512 tokens or 2s whichever first, then flush as legacy batch for non-streaming clients
Return HTTP 206 for partial stream completion when downstream reranker times out; include X-Legacy-Partial: true header
open_questions: Should we attempt lossy conversion of function-calling hints into legacy 'metadata' tags or simply drop them and emit warnings?
What SLAs do we guarantee for cursor expiration vs. legacy expiration? Current ask is 72h but PMs may request 7d for large customers
How to surface migration troubleshooting to customers who still call legacy endpoints? Provide a migration endpoint that validates client payloads?
